JUDGMENT The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 20.06.2021.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner as follows:
On 20.06.2021 at about 07.00 a.m. while petitioner was proceeding in his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-HX-7195 to Rachenahalli Main road and when he reached in front of A to Z Aparts Sandalwood studio road, Thinisandra, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the Maxi Cab bearing Reg. No.KA- 05-AF-3913 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle and as a result,
petitioner sustained injuries.

Immediately, petitioner was shifted to North Bengaluru hospital, wherein first aid treatment given and then shifted to Dr. Ambedkar College hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment for his accidental injuries as an inpatient.

It is stated that he has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment,
medicine etc.,
3.
It is further stated that prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as a car driver and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work as doing earlier.
It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the Maxi Cab bearing Reg. No. KA-05- AF-3913.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending Max cab are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its learned counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and hence, he was placed exparte.
5. The 2nd respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.

It has denied the age,

It is contended that the insured of the offending vehicle has violated Section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3.

On the other hand, respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence on its behalf.

The petitioner in order to prove his case, got examined himself as PW.1 and reiterated the averments of the petition and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, Spot Sketch,Spot mahazar, Notice under Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply to notice under Sec.133 of IMV Act, IMV report, Wound certificate and Charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.
11.
The version of the petitioners remains unchallenged and undisputed.
But mere unchallenged and undisputed facts does not amounts to proof of the same.
The petitioner is bestowed with the burden to prove the specific assertions in the light of oral and documentary proof.
12. This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of car.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty:
For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages:
At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

13. According to the version of petitioner, the accident happened in front of A to Z Aparts Sandalwood studio road, Thinisandra, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the Max cab bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF-3913 came from opposite side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle and caused the accident.

sentences.text: The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.4 being the Spot Mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 and 4 which are the Spot Mahazar and Sketch it reflects that the injured was proceeding in a motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-HX-7195, the driver of the Max cab bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF-3913 came from opposite side in a negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle.

As per this document accident occurred on left side of the road, width of the road is 20 feet, which makes it clear that the driver of maxi cab without observing on going vehicle dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle.
The said factum is also fortified with the IMV report.
If the driver of the Maxi cab bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF- 3913 drove it in a normal speed by observing on going vehicles on the road, then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Added more, the contents of the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle and also right side of both vehicle damaged.
Further more, even the chargesheet as per Ex.P9 was also filed as against the rider of the offending motor cycle.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P3,4 coupled with Ex.P9 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the Bolero Maxi cab.
14. Even in the instant case the driver of the Maxi cab is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part.

After the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending Maxi cab bearing registration Reg. No.KA-05-AF-3913 concluding that the accident was occurred only due to his negligence.
There is no reason to take a different view.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the offending Maxi cab bearing Reg. No. KA-05-AF- 3913.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Maxi cab bearing Reg. No. KA-05-AF-3913.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.

16. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
It is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was working as Car driver and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and to prove the same, petitioner has not produced any documents.
In the absence of document of income, the tribunal has to consider the notional income of the petitioner.
The incident occurred during the year 2021.
considering the avocation and the year of the accident, I deem it just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/- per month.
The petitioner claims that he is unable to work due to the injuries sustained to him.
The petitioner got examined the Doctor as PW.2.
In the evidence of doctor, he has deposed that petitioner sustained open mid shaft right leg both bones fracture.
On examination he found that the petitioner has healed scar over the right knee, wasting of the right thigh muscles, restricted right knee and ankle movements.

He assessed 42% disability to the Right Lower Limb and 14% whole body disability of the Raja Hussain vs Yashavantha Raje Urs on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72677161/

sentences.text: While calculating the loss of future income on account of permanent disability, the functional disability to the whole body has to be considered.
The disability to the whole body shall have to be assessed on the basis of the profession of the injured and relative effect of the disability to his profession.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are not in dispute and the injuries sustained by him definitely will have an impact on his work.
PW.2 is not a treated doctor and the disability assessed by him has to be taken into consideration carefully.
Hence, considering the nature of the work and impact of disability on his performance, I deem it just and proper to consider 12% disability to his whole body.
It is contended that petitioner was aged 49 years as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 20.06.2021.
However, by considering the date of birth mentioned in Ex.P13 and Ex.P14 Adhaar card and DL as 01.06.1971, the petitioner was aged 50 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 50 is 13 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).

17. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
As per wound certificate produced at Ex.P8, the petitioner has sustained fracture both bones Right leg and fracture distal phalanx of right middle finger.

The Ex.P10 Discharge Summary of Dr. Ambedkar Medical College and Hospital reveals that the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the said hospital from 20.06.2021 to 01.11.2021 and took conservative treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.50,000/- towards pain and sufferings.
18. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced medical bills worth Rs.1,95,548/- at Ex.P11.

sentences.text: Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.50,000/- under this head.

20. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least five months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.75,000/- (15,000X5) under this head.

21. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The petitioner was aged about 50 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
He has to suffer this discomfort and sacrifice the amenities through out his remaining life.
This court has considered disability to the extent of 12% to whole body.
Considering all these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.40,000/- on this head.
22. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
The doctor stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implant which may cost Rs.60,000/-.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
Petitioner has to undergo surgery of removal of implant, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.30,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.

The petitioner is claiming interest on the compensation amount.
The respondents have denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount excluding the future medical expenses.
25. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Maxi cab bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-AF-3913.
In the written statement, respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy and its validity in respect of the offending vehicle.
Further, the respondent No.2 has not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, 1 st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2nd respondent being the insurer shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
26. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,18,808/-(Rupees Seven lakhs eighteen thousand eight hundred and eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on Rs.6,88,808/- (excluding future expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the compensation amount, 60% of the award amount shall be paid to him through E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 40% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 2 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
